# storefront release bundle

The storefront release ships message catalogs and database changes together.
Keep locale coverage complete and make every schema revision reversible before
the bundle is deployed.

## Project layout

    ./
    ├─ catalogs/                        locale-specific message catalogs
    │  │
    │  └─ [locale]/                     (zero or more matching directories)
    │     │
    │     ├─ checkout.json              the checkout message catalog for one
    │     │                             locale (required)
    │     │
    │     └─ [domain].json              a message catalog for one locale and
    │                                   domain (zero or more matching files)
    │
    └─ migrations/                      reversible storefront schema changes
       │
       ├─ baseline.sql                  the idempotent initial storefront schema
       │                                (required)
       │
       └─ [revision].{up.sql,down.sql}  a forward or rollback schema migration
                                        (zero or more matching files)

## `catalogs/` — locale-specific message catalogs

Each locale has JSON catalogs for its application domains. Checkout is
required for every locale and has its own message requirements. The rules
below cover shipped copy, legal text, and consistency across locales.

### `[locale]/checkout.json` — the checkout message catalog for one locale

Each locale has a checkout catalog with non-empty plain-text
messages for pay_now, payment_failed, and order_confirmed. The checkout UI
uses these IDs directly and does not render HTML from catalog values.

### `[locale]/[domain].json` — a message catalog for one locale and domain

Each domain catalog is a JSON object from message IDs to
non-empty strings. Its filename is the domain identifier used by the storefront.

### checkout-keys — checkout message IDs agree across locales

Together, paths matching `*/checkout.json` under `catalogs/` must follow this
rule.

All checkout catalogs expose the same message IDs.
Values differ by locale, but the checkout UI can use one stable key set.

### domain-coverage — every locale covers the same domains

Together, files with exactly `.json` as their extension under `catalogs/` must
follow this rule.

Every locale represented in the catalog tree has the same
set of domain files. A missing domain leaves part of the storefront untranslated.

### legal-no-markup — legal copy stays plain text

Each path matching `*/legal-*.json` under `catalogs/` must follow this rule.

Every legal-* catalog contains plain-text legal copy,
never HTML markup. Legal screens render its values without HTML parsing.

### no-placeholder-copy — shipped copy has no editorial placeholders

Each file with exactly `.json` as its extension under `catalogs/` must follow
this rule.

No catalog ships TODO or TBD as display copy. Finish each
message in its language before publishing the catalog.

## `migrations/` — reversible storefront schema changes

The baseline creates a fresh storefront database. Later numbered revisions
ship a forward and rollback script as a pair. All SQL in this directory is
reviewed as part of the same release bundle as the catalogs.

### `baseline.sql` — the idempotent initial storefront schema

The baseline establishes the tables needed by a fresh
storefront installation. It is a standalone .sql file, not one side of a
numbered migration pair.

### `[revision].{up.sql,down.sql}` — a forward or rollback schema migration

Each numbered revision has an up script and a down script.
Keep the revision number in both filenames; the pair check verifies that both
directions are present.

### bootstrap-idempotent — standalone SQL can be reapplied safely

Each file with exactly `.sql` as its extension under `migrations/` must follow
this rule.

Standalone SQL scripts, such as the initial baseline,
use CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS so rerunning setup does not fail. Numbered
up and down migrations have different lifecycle rules.

### migration-pairs — every schema revision has both directions

Together, files whose names end in `.down.sql` or `.up.sql` under `migrations/`
must follow this rule.

Every numbered schema revision ships exactly one forward
script and one rollback script. A release without either direction cannot be
applied and reverted reliably.

### no-destructive-up — forward migrations preserve existing tables

Each file with exactly `.up.sql` as its extension under `migrations/` must
follow this rule.

Forward migrations must not drop a table. If a release
retires data, use a separately reviewed cleanup after readers have moved.

### no-sql-placeholders — release SQL has no unfinished edits

Each file whose name ends in `.sql` under `migrations/` must follow this rule.

No SQL shipped in this release bundle contains a TODO or
TBD marker. This applies to the standalone baseline and to both directions
of every numbered migration.

### transaction-boundaries — numbered migrations run in a transaction

Each file with exactly `.up.sql` or `.down.sql` as its extension under
`migrations/` must follow this rule.

Each numbered migration begins with a header naming its
revision and direction, then runs between BEGIN and COMMIT. The standalone
baseline follows its own setup contract.

Every path in this directory must fit the project layout or a documented
repository-specific purpose.

## Working with Espalier

Espalier is the architecture compiler for this repository. It turns structural
rules and `ESPALIER.MD` guidance into this generated document, then checks the
working tree against them. Use it to place new code, discover the constraints on
a path, and catch architectural drift while a change is still small.

`espalier help` prints this CLI version's manual. With no page it lists every
page.

Use this loop:

1. Find the intended path in **Project layout** and read the generated guidance
   in the nearest directory.
2. Run `espalier explain <path>` when you need to understand how a path is
   governed.
3. Inspect creation options with `espalier create <path> help`, then create the
   declared file or complete required directory with `espalier create <path>`.
   A required file without a custom template starts empty.
4. Make the remaining change without working around the declared structure.
5. Run `espalier lint` and follow the rule text attached to each finding.
6. Run `espalier build`, review and include any generated guidance changes,
   then run `espalier build --check` immediately before committing.

Generated guidance files are outputs, not edit targets. When a task explicitly
changes the architecture, update the corresponding `ESPALIER.MD` for guidance
or the structural rule modules for structure, then run `espalier build`.
Otherwise, if the work has no valid place or conflicts with a rule, report the
design gap instead of weakening the espalier. Use `espalier build --force` only
to restore a generated file whose provenance marker was removed; it authorizes
overwriting an unmarked document at a planned output path.
